_note: Marginal-buyer constraint cards (WS1.4): the regulatory/structural rules that bind the institutions whose forced selling or buying-strike transmits AI-DC credit stress. Compiled 2026-06-12 from web research; tiers: statute|agency|press|estimate. These complete the funding map into a timing mechanism and feed the verdict tree's funding-first pathway (src/bubble/verdict_tree.py, pathway B) and signals S2/S3. Prose + full cites: analysis/marginal_buyer_constraints.md. sec.gov not fetched; some figures corroborated via secondary sources (flagged).
chain: AI-DC SPV/neocloud debt -> private-credit originators (Blackstone, Blue Owl, Apollo, PIMCO, BlackRock, Ares) -> rated notes/ABS/CLO tranches -> held by life-insurer general accounts (~$2.5T annuities), BDCs (~$407B private-credit investments), and semi-liquid funds; affiliated-structure leverage up to ~12:1, ~$95B committed bank lines.

scale_anchor.private_credit_to_ai: ~$0 -> >$200B (~8% of all private credit); $40B+ originated 2025; projected $300-600B by 2030
scale_anchor.data_center_financing: Morgan Stanley: private credit could supply >half of ~$1.5T DC financing through 2028

1_insurer_rbc.binding_constraint: NAIC C-1 RBC charge steps up nonlinearly as designation worsens

trigger_levels.proposed_clo_thickness_cliff: Baa3 tranche 2.73% -> 12.52% if <=4% of CLO capital (not adopted Spring 2026; ~end-2027)

1_insurer_rbc.mechanical_consequence: No automatic forced sale: SSAP 26R holds at amortized cost up to NAIC 5 (mark only at NAIC 6). The bite is the higher RBC charge, measured at year-end -> first insurer move is a BUYERS' STRIKE, not forced selling, until a downgrade hits the nonlinear cliff.
1_insurer_rbc.speed: slowest, largest balance sheet, highest severity if the cliff is hit
1_insurer_rbc.tier: statute (NAIC factors, SSAP 26R); agency (Milliman, Academy, IMF GFSR via Institutional Investor)

2_bdc_leverage.binding_constraint: 150% asset-coverage minimum = 2:1 debt:equity (ICA s61(a)/s18, 2018 SBCAA); but bank facilities/borrowing bases bind FAR earlier

trigger_levels.borrowing_base_bite: 5-10% mark declines already force paydowns/dividend pressure long before statutory breach
trigger_levels.current_posture_jun2026: 8 rated non-traded BDCs avg 0.85x leverage; severe-stress 1.39x, still < 2.0x

2_bdc_leverage.mechanical_consequence: Below the floor: cannot issue new debt, cannot pay certain distributions, must delever (sell assets) or raise equity, risks RIC tax status. The real edge is the continuous >=150% bank covenant + advance-rate haircuts -> a redemption wave + AI-collateral marks converts into forced delevering here.
2_bdc_leverage.speed: second; the first place a mark-down becomes a forced sale
2_bdc_leverage.tier: statute (SBCAA, s18); estimate (breach % derivations); agency (KBRA, Fitch)

3_annuity_surrender.binding_constraint: surrenderable liabilities can run faster than illiquid private credit can be sold (disintermediation)
3_annuity_surrender.mechanical_consequence: A rate/confidence shock -> surrender wave -> insurer must sell long-duration/illiquid bonds at depressed value. Surrender charges + MVA deliberately slow this -> the deepest channel but the last to break.
3_annuity_surrender.tier: agency (Fed FEDS Notes, AM Best); statute (NAIC); estimate (surrender-protected inverse)

4_semiliquid_gates.binding_constraint: quarterly redemption gate (typically 5% of NAV/qtr, ~20%/yr) with mandatory proration when exceeded

trigger_levels.unfilled_remainder: NOT carried over; holders re-tender next quarter

gates_actually_hit_2026.BCRED_Q1_2026: 7.9% of NAV (~$3.7B) requested; board upsized to 7%, sponsor covered last ~0.9% -> 100% met
gates_actually_hit_2026.BCRED_Q2_2026: ~10% of shares (2x cap); held 5% -> first BCRED gate; ~50% prorated (derived)
gates_actually_hit_2026.BlueOwl_OTIC_Q1_2026: 40.7% of shares requested vs 5% cap -> ~12% prorated

4_semiliquid_gates.mechanical_consequence: Requests above the cap are prorated; the unfilled remainder forces re-tender, eroding confidence. FSB (May 2026): meeting requests at the limit 'may also have stimulated further redemption pressures' -- gates RATION and SIGNAL stress, they do not dissipate it.
4_semiliquid_gates.speed: fastest; ALREADY BINDING in 2026 on AI-credit-exposed vehicles
4_semiliquid_gates.tier: statute (Rule 23c-3); press (PitchBook, Reuters, CNBC, AltsWire); agency (FSB, IMF GFSR)

first_transmission_channel.answer: semi-liquid-fund redemption gates -- and they are already binding in 2026 (Apollo 45%, Ares 43.1%, Blue Owl OTIC 40.7% requested, BCRED first gate Q2-2026), explicitly amid 'AI fears'
ordering: 1. fund redemption gates (fastest, live now): retail flight -> proration -> re-tender -> confidence erosion; procyclical per FSB
2. BDC bank-facility/borrowing-base tightening (second, mark-driven): 5-10% marks force paydowns -- where a mark-down becomes a forced sale
3. insurer RBC downgrade cliff (slower, largest balance sheet, highest severity): buyers' strike first, then the nonlinear cliff if downgraded
4. annuity surrender/disintermediation (slowest, deepest tail): 55% withdrawable vs ~6% liquid buffer, but surrender charges slow it
first_transmission_channel.coupling_risk: the same managers (Apollo, Blackstone, Blue Owl, Ares) run the gated funds, the BDCs, AND the insurers' affiliated asset management -- so stress starting as retail redemptions + bank-line tightening lands on the same balance sheets holding the rated-note AI-DC paper, at ~12:1 affiliated leverage.
